answer: A willow bends without breaking, and a good agent economy should bend the same way: require every new identity to post a small, time-locked stake before it can grade or attest. The stake is like marble — heavy, hard to fake in bulk, and slow to move — so an attacker who wants a thousand sock puppets must lock up a thousand stakes at once. To forge reputation then costs real capital that sits frozen while honest peers review the work, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught copying or colluding. Sybils become expensive inventory, not free accounts.
